what: SIM-388/SIM-393 review: collapsed event marks switch events; synthetic inspection has read-only navigation. Completed checklist rows have no optional controls; compact phone actions sit below labels, and Home header actions have their own row. Walkthrough copy follows checklist actions and the current Settings destinations.

SIM-393 slice 2: shared server checklist on organiser and judge Home; optional item restore, rubric final/read and conflict acknowledgements; participant entry rows retain their exact appearance. Prototypes use the built checklist markup and earlier-work groups.

SIM-388/SIM-393 navigation slice 1: persistent event pane without the duplicate desktop switcher; grouped organiser activities, Settings sections and Event page Tracks; membership abilities and organiser judging. Quiet Home header actions and compact optional prototype rows. Checklist implementation remains slice 2.

SIM-388/SIM-393 gated review: persistent event pane and Home arrival; shared navigation.json generates role nav. Organiser Set up / Run / Wrap up; Event page keeps its tabs plus Tracks, Settings collects rules and administration, exports stay put. Stage checklists, optional Not needed, judge rubric/conflict acknowledgements, organiser judge-area state, current/past events and compatibility aliases. Atlas and design only; application work follows in two slices.

Owner: one name per person, not one per event. public-join, public-apply, public-judge and public-organiser-invite ask for a name only when the signed-in account has none yet; the server saves it as the account's display name (Account's existing field, not a new one). An account that already has a name sees a read-only 'You'll appear as <name>. Change it on Account.' line instead of an input, and the request never sends display_name. public-organiser-invite no longer invents a name from the email prefix or falls back to the literal 'Co-organiser'. Account's Name help text now says the name is shown in every event, and a rename there updates it everywhere (teams, organisers, judges, results) -- organiser-people's rows read from the same one name. Prototype: public-join, public-apply~form, public-judge, public-organiser-invite, account, plus new ~no-name states for public-join, public-apply, public-judge and public-organiser-invite showing the empty-account input.

SIM-379: Event Basics reuses the schedule date and time pickers. An empty time still means local midnight in the event zone, same as before -- a midnight end still lasts the whole of that day. Each pair fills the phone width. Event dates show a time only when it isn't midnight.

SIM-382 (owner): the entry-rules preset picker narrows to two -- Video or website (the default) and Video, website and code link; AI build, Coding, Ideas and design and Custom drop out of the picker (an event already on one keeps its own rules). organiser-overview gains a new first step for a brand-new event, 'Choose what teams hand in' (next_step.kind entry_rules), before Open sign-up is offered; saving any choice, even the default, moves it on. Prototype: organiser-entries(~empty, ~confirm), organiser-overview~entry-rules (new).

Owner: there is exactly one way to connect an AI app, the MCP address; Get started drops every plugin, plugin-ZIP and connector-directory mention. Account gained a Connect your AI app card (address, Claude/ChatGPT/Claude Code steps, link to other apps, GET /v1/me/connections status); the old AI apps note said there was nothing to set up here, now there is. The Website screen's publish card gained a Claude Code tab. Prototype: account, participant-website(~unpublished, ~connected).

Notices extension: judge-home gets a Needs you card (judging_open/judging_reminder, section queue, needsCard/bindDismiss). Organiser team-detail gets a Messages card (sent history, 'No messages sent to this team yet.') with a Message team button (textarea, 1000-character counter, hidden once archived); organiser-teams' Teams tab gets per-row checkboxes and a Message selected button (1 to 25, shared dialog via _team-message-dialog.js). participant-team's Members tab gets a Messages from the organisers card, hidden when empty. organiser-entries gets a Reminder times card (removable chips, an add control in minutes/hours/days, 5 max, 15 min to 14 days, Save; reads/writes GET/PUT .../reminders) -- Entries, not Settings, since it already owns the deadline these reminders key off. organiser-judging gets a Judging closes card (plain date-time, PATCH judging_ends_at) next to the rubric and tie-break, per the CHANGE 2026-11-05 note dropping schedule-row inference; schedule.js's setInLink/soonText/cueHeading learn the fixed row key judging_end. New features: judge-needs-you, judging-reminder-email, message-team, view-team-messages, view-messages-from-organisers, set-reminder-times, set-judging-closes. New FEATURES.md anchors: judge-notices, team-messages, reminder-times. Prototype: judge-home, organiser-team-detail(~message), organiser-teams, participant-team~with-team, organiser-entries, organiser-judging.

Self-hosted installs may enable password accounts. The shared sign-in card offers username/email and password after providers, account creation when enabled, and a new-password field for temporary credentials. Hosted services keep their current methods. Prototype: public-apply~password.

Entries slice 3 built: publishing and showing. participant-website: a state strip (AI app: Not connected / Connected in Claude, last used, teammates connected too / Connected to another team with a switch line / Using a key; Website: Not published yet / Published, version, when, link), Claude and ChatGPT tabs (default: the app last connected) with numbered steps read from hack-connect-steps.json, which /get-started now renders too, the person's sign-in email named, a Copy prompt built from the entry, and polling every 5 s for up to 10 minutes while visible with a toast on Connected and Published; once published the steps fold into Publish again. public-event-page: results rows carry the summary card (winners open, other full-ranking rows folded), Open website / Watch video (host named, never embedded) / View code when the event asks for it, only on rows the results setting shows; team site cards gain tool tags and See result. participant-results: Your entry as the public sees it, or one line saying it is not shown. Deadline reminder email 24 h and 1 h before for teams not submitted (Account email switch respected, never key-only accounts).

Entries slice 2 built: the judge's one screen (judge-scoring). The card is the page header, then the video and the website in the event's judge_first order, then code and More detail. The video plays here only from the server-built video.embed_url (YouTube via youtube-nocookie, Vimeo, Loom, Drive), after the judge presses play; anything else is a host-named link. The website is the server's preview_url framed in a sandbox when site.frameable, else the screenshot, a one-line reason (passcode, named viewers, offline, taken down) and Open website. Right column: n of m scored with a bar, each criterion's weight, the unscored guard line on Save & next (a second press within 10 seconds moves on), the conflict button in a Know this team? box, and N / P keys. Only the judge route gets the wider frame-src. judge-queue rows gain track and maturity pills. The MCP App judge view shows the card with links, no embeds. The scoring walkthrough gains card and video steps.

A schedule that acts (feature audit item 10, owner-agreed 2026-11-02). Real times now appear in the schedule by themselves as fixed rows that can't drift: event start and end (All day when the date has no time), the entry deadline (a participant's own team extension in their view), the voting window and results published. The server computes them from the settings on every read (GET /content fixed_schedule, the public feed, the built-in page) and never stores them. On Event page > Schedule each fixed row has a Fixed pill and a 'Set in Basics/Entries/Results' link instead of Edit. A typed row can be set to ask for a next step when it starts ('When this starts, ask to'), and the entry deadline always asks to close entries. Overview's next step then reads e.g. 'Kickoff is now. Open sign-up?' or 'Entries were due at 6:00 pm. Close entries?' with 'From your schedule. Nothing changes until you press Close entries.' The stage never moves by itself. Participant Home and Schedule show one line when a row starts within 15 minutes or is on now ('Demos starts in 12 minutes', 'Build time is on now'), in the app only with no email (deadline reminder emails are separate). Prototypes: organiser-event-page~schedule and ~schedule-add, participant-schedule, participant-home~starting-soon, organiser-overview~schedule-cue and ~deadline-passed, public-event-page. Judges: no change (decision recorded on judge-home).

Notify people when something waits on them (audit item 7, built 2026-11-02). A participant's Home gains a Needs you card above the next-step card: team requests and invites, a request or application answered, a team or site change, and a new admin, each a live row that clears itself or a dismissable news row, kept for up to 14 days. Organiser Overview gains a Needs you line when applications are waiting, linking to People; the same count already drove the People badge. Home across every event gains its own Needs you card, each row named for its event. The participant Team, Overview and Announcements badges and the organiser People badge now have documented rules (pending requests plus invites, unseen news, unread-since-last-visit, pending applications). A removed participant sees the existing team-removal notice on Team as well as Home. Decision emails now go out for all of this, on by default with one Account opt-out ('Email me when something waits on me'), batched to at most one email per kind every 15 minutes; organisers hear applicant counts by email, never names; a locked team stays in-app only; leaving still sends nothing. New API: GET /v1/hack/todos, POST /v1/hack/events/{slug}/notices/seen, and needs_you on the event read. New MCP: hack_get_my_todos, hack_dismiss_notices, hack_set_email_updates.

Entries and participant journey (audit top 4, 5, 6, 8, 9), designed, not built. Entry gets a fixed summary card (problem, solution = the existing tagline, who it's for, track = the team's track, tools and AI tags with suggestions, what works today) with a live 'How judges see it' preview, and an explicit Submit that enforces the event's rules (drafts save freely; a complete draft submits itself at the deadline, an incomplete one isn't judged). Entries replaces the required-field ticks with three presets (AI build, Coding, Ideas and design) and per-line Required / One of / Optional / Off, a Video-or-Website-first choice for judges, counts and per-team status. Judge scoring puts the card, a click-to-load video (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom, Drive) and a framed preview of the submitted site on one screen beside the rubric, with weights, an unscored guard and N / P keys. Participant Home becomes the next step plus a four-step checklist with a live countdown to the team's own deadline. Website guides Claude, ChatGPT and other apps step by step and shows Connected (from the connector grant's selected team) and Published. Public results and the team sites list show each shown team's card, site and video link. New prototype kit rules live in prototype/kit-next.css until built. 22 new features.

Feature audit fixes 1 and 2 (3, guardian consent, dropped by owner decision -- events are for school and college students, organisers handle consent themselves). Teams can see the rubric: an approved participant can now read the event's rubric (criteria, descriptions, weights, max points, never a score) via a new 'How you're judged' card on participant-entry, linked from Home -- GET /v1/hack/events/{slug}/rubric accepts the participant role, no response-shape change, no organiser setting to hide it, hack_get_rubric works the same way over MCP. Panel judging warns before dropping untracked teams: in panel mode a team with no track matches no panel and gets no judges (internal/db/hack_judging_options.go); organiser-judging's Progress card and organiser-overview's next-step card (before Start judging) now name every such team with a link to Teams, and the Start judging confirm repeats the count -- all computed client-side from GET .../teams and GET .../judging/settings, data those screens already fetch, so no server or schema change. New atlas feature ids view-rubric-participant and warn-teams-without-track; new prototype states organiser-overview~closed and organiser-judging~panel-untracked.

Grok SIM-346 re-test fixes, round 6 plus the five round-5 items still open. Leave: the Overview danger-zone row and the Leave dialog now share one text builder (leave.js participantWarning), fixing the lone-member row that wrongly promised 'teammates keep the team' when leaving actually deletes it, and 'keep'/'keeps' now agrees with how many teammates remain. ui.possessive's own apostrophe rule was already right (’s / bare ’ for a name ending in s); the bug was call sites hand-building "'s" instead of using it -- fixed in the leave copy, the Remove member dialog and the Delete-scores dialog. Delete scores (a former judge) now takes a typed confirm (the event's address name, same pattern as Settings' Delete event; the server already required confirm=slug) via a new ui.confirmTyped. Remove member asks its question once, in the title. Team Members header on both the participant and organiser screens drops 'Admins decide who joins' (it contradicted the Team link card's own 'joins straight away' right below it) for one rule: 'Anyone with the team link joins straight away. Admins approve requests to join.' Team Settings sub-heading drops the removed 'who can join' setting. In-event URLs for a non-member (left, removed, or never joined) now say 'You're not in <event>', not 'Event not found', by falling back to the credential-less public feed when the member-scoped GET 404s. An organiser or judge opening a participant's /team link now redirects to their own area again (nav.js's resolveRoute exposes the URL's implied role, app.js's route() compares it to the real event.role). The public event page's sign-in prompt is gone for a signed-in non-member, but the body used to still say 'sign in with your email' -- it now shows Apply (if the page already rendered one) or 'Ask the organisers for the join link'. kit.css Form layout gains one rule for a dialog title's gap above its first field (ui.dialog()'s own h2, used by every formDialog -- Add track, Fill teams, the schedule, sponsor and FAQ dialogs), fixing all of them at once instead of per dialog.

Overview, top bar and Teams redesigned (owner, 2026-10-31, not built yet). Overview's next-step card holds ONE button that performs the next forward move after a confirm (Open sign-up, Start building, Close entries, Start judging, Finish judging, Publish results, End event), its other buttons are gone, and Change stage stays in the header. Moving to Results now locks judging. Participants and judges see the event's stage in the top bar in the same words as organisers, with the stage track on their home screen, and judges keep a scoring pill beside it. Teams: the 'Who can join' setting is gone, every team has one link that joins in one confirm (/team/{code}), the no-team page asks 'How do you want to team up?' with three choices instead of two side-by-side boxes, and an on-team Team area has Members, Find people and Settings sub-pages. Whoever starts a team is its admin, admins approve requests, lock the team, rename it, remove members, make admins and make a new link, and the longest-standing member takes over when the last admin leaves. The organiser's Teams screen gets Teams, Not on a team, Tracks and Settings sub-pages, Fill teams asks how many people per team, and the default team size is 20.

Form layout overhaul (owner: labels flush against their selects, misaligned across screens). kit.css now has one Form layout block, the only place form spacing and alignment live: .field stacks label, control, help and error on a 6px grid gap (a label that wraps its control gets the same gap, so older and DOM-built markup is fixed by CSS too), .field.inline puts a short label beside its control (the People Show filter, tied-rank places) and stacks on phone, .check aligns the box with the first text line and indents help under the label, .field-row and .control-row keep every input, select and the buttons beside them at one 40px height, and .form-actions gives every Save row the same 16px above it. Spacing tokens --field-gap, --label-gap, --control-h and friends sit on :root. Results, Judging, People, Teams, Team detail, Entries, Settings, Account, Create event, Announcements, Event page, the participant Team, Entry and Website screens, the public apply, join and judge-invite pages and the voting settings page now use these classes, and their one-off style attributes are gone. BUILD.md has the patterns under Form layout.

Announcement email reporting fixed (organiser-announcements): the post result and the Posted list now report the server's real counts instead of a guess from the event's participant total. The checkbox reads 'Email N participants' (N = approved participants with an email-shaped username), disabled with 'No participant has an email address yet.' at zero; the Post button still names the send on itself. Posting reports 'Posted and emailed to N people' from the response's real emails_queued, or, at zero, the warning 'Posted. Nobody had an email address on file, so no email was sent.' Ticking the box also queues one copy to the posting organiser when their own username is email-shaped, named '(including a copy to you)' in the result, never a duplicate if they're also a participant. Each posted row's pill now reads 'Emailed N people' from emails_sent (deliveries actually sent, not merely queued), replacing the dropped pill a stale comment explained away.

Leave this event widened twice (SIM-340, owner decisions 2026-10-31): past a team's deadline, or once the event is closed, judging or results, leaving no longer refuses -- it just stops touching the team, its entry, its site and its scores, even for the last member, instead of deleting an emptied team or blocking the leave outright; the preview and confirm say so ('<team>'s entry and site stay as they are... you can't rejoin this team'), and the participant-home leave-blocked state is gone for participants (an ended event still refuses everyone). Separately, a rejected applicant can now leave too, deleting their row exactly like a pending applicant's withdraw, with no special refusal and no extra machinery stopping them from applying again -- the Home row menu and the pending/rejected locked view both offer it. Judging, the judge queue, the results snapshot and the organiser's auto-assignment all keep listing a frozen, now-empty team exactly as before, so results and ranks never move.

Fixes from Grok's fourth production test (SIM-346): the public event page tells a pending applicant their application is waiting for the organisers, with a way to see it, and a rejected one that it wasn't accepted, instead of both reading 'You've already joined'; a signed-in visitor who isn't a member of the event no longer sees 'Already joined? Sign in'; the vote page explains 'No teams to vote for yet' instead of going blank when no team has a live site yet; the judge 'I know someone' confirm names the team (not the entry title), matching the undo dialog, and only mentions a score stopping when the judge actually scored that team; Results no longer shows an empty Publish card once there is nothing to show under it; country names fall back to English when the browser's own locale tag is one Intl.DisplayNames can't parse (e.g. 'en-US@posix'), instead of falling all the way to the bare code; People -> Everyone reads a pending applicant's date as 'Applied', not 'Joined'.

Leave this event designed (SIM-340, not built yet): a danger-zone Leave on the participant and judge Overview and in organiser Settings, plus a … menu on each Home row, all driven by one preview of what leaving does. Participants leave their team first (a lone member's team, entry and site go) and can't leave once their team's deadline passes, pending applicants withdraw, rejected ones can't leave. Judges' scores stay and keep counting, and Judging gets a 'Left the event' row with Delete scores. The creator hands the event to a co-organiser, the last organiser ends or deletes it. Ended events show Leave disabled with the reason. Owner decisions 2026-10-30, the rest decided in the atlas.

Fixes from Grok's third production test (SIM-346): judge My teams rows stack on phone; Team finding stays open with Saved; participant Team saves show Saved; the Fill teams preview says when a code-only team with room was skipped; people who can't vote see why up front and no active Vote button; Your details shows Saved; Create event address messages are friendly; scoring says No entry was submitted once; the scoring walkthrough's comment step sits beside the score rows; the I know someone undo only promises a score that exists; You are on <team> now shows once per placement; Results after End groups the still-live Publish, listing and downloads before the read-only note; the public event page offers Continue to your event to someone already in.

Apply is only for events listed in Find a hackathon. An unlisted event's public page shows no Apply, its apply page shows the applications-off state, and Settings says the event must be listed in Results first (owner decision).

Apply to a hackathon: people without a join link can apply from Find a hackathon (Apply on a listed event's row) and from the event's public page, at a new public-apply screen (/e/{slug}/apply). The form asks name and email from sign-in, optional city and country, age range and gender, then the event's own questions and the code of conduct, with a line saying only the organisers see the answers. Every application waits in People -> Applications, now with email, how they came, location, age range (Under 18 highlighted) and gender, filters by source, age range and country, and those fields in the participants CSV. Applications are on by default; Settings has one switch to turn them off. The approval toggle now only governs join-link sign-ups, and admit-everyone-waiting never admits applications. Join links are unchanged and stay private. Owner decisions, 2026-10-31.

Event page redesigned as seven sub-pages shown one at a time, each with its own address (?s=event-page&tab=basics|about|schedule|sponsors|faq|look|website), landing on Basics: forms with one Save in the card foot, lists of rows with a quiet Edit and a … menu (move, remove with Undo) and add/edit in a dialog, file pickers as buttons with a preview, colour as swatches, a live preview on Look, and Website (address, built-in vs own site, zip upload, versions) split from Look. Schedule lost its reorder control because every view sorts it by time. Announcements became their own organiser sidebar section under Event page. New kit rhythm and button-placement rules (shell.layout_rules, kit.css), and a desktop sidebar that folds into a remembered icon rail with tooltips. Owner, 2026-10-30: 'Only show Basics when I click Basics, only Schedule when I click Schedule. This looks like a band-aid fix, clean it up.'

Sign out moved to the sidebar foot (Account, Sign out, Help; on phone in the Menu sheet), one tap from any screen; the Account page's one-button Session card is gone, and Sign out everywhere stays in its Danger zone. Owner, 2026-10-30: Sign out was in the wrong place; decided by the ux-arbiter.

Added a home level above the event: the sidebar's top-left is now the Simple Hack wordmark plus the signed-in person's name, leading to Home (/events) from any screen; the event switcher moved one level down to head a second sidebar section (current event + role) that only appears while an event is open -- on Home itself only the top section (Home, Find a hackathon) shows. landing-your-events is now Home, a real page: events grouped by what needs the person first, each row with role, stage and a plain next action built from that data (no invented counts), plus Find a hackathon, Create event and Account, with an empty state for a brand-new account. The judge and participant 'Home' nav section is renamed 'Overview' everywhere (label, title, phone tab, breadcrumbs, walkthrough copy) so 'Home' means only the person's own home; URLs are unchanged (?s=home still works). Owner, 2026-10-30: 'the top-left should lead to my home, the event is one level below.'

Fixed the judge walkthrough: Home no longer explains the scoring page from two untargeted steps that showed even after results were out -- Home now only covers Home (welcome, status, next-step block, progress, My teams, Rubric & brief, Help), the status step is stage-aware (open / opens-later / nothing at all once locked or results are out), and a new judgeScoring tour auto-starts on the scoring page itself once scoring is open, pointing at the team site link, first score buttons, comment box, Save & next, and I know someone on this team. Added matching walkthroughs for participants: tours.participant on Home (sidebar items, next-step block) and tours.participantTeam on Team (open teams, start/join a team, Be found), auto-starting for an approved participant / a solo participant while teams are open. Seen-state for every new tour is localStorage (no server preference field exists for them).

Public event page redesigned in the app's calm kit style instead of the ink look, still themed by the event colour and icon: the block under the header now does the stage's one job (how to join, time left, see team sites, vote, results first), sections reorder by who reads the page at each stage, 'On this page' chips and collapsed sections shorten the phone page, link previews get a title and description, and invented gallery status tags and a 'results expected' date were removed. 15 states, 7 prototype states, 11 feature ideas and 5 questions for the domain expert.

Added the guided walkthrough for organisers and judges: a non-modal card that points at the real Overview/Home elements (status, Change stage, share links, Score next, progress, Help), replacing the old screen-covering modal tour and the static toggle panels on organiser-overview and judge-home. Shown once automatically, replayed from Help, saved to the same organiser_walkthrough_done/judge_walkthrough_done preference the old tour used.

Judge screens after an independent walkthrough as a first-time, non-technical judge on a phone (7/10): 'I know this team' now confirms visibly, score buttons are thumb-sized, a jump to scoring on phones, a 'You're done' Home, and plainer words (My teams, Teams I know).

Design review of the rendered prototype: organiser pages get a real header with one main action, the Judging page leads with progress and Lock while judging is live, the rubric is edited as rows, per-row delete buttons are quiet instead of red boxes, and 4 copy errors are corrected against the code.

Atlas rebuilt as a living spec: app shell for every role, 32 screens designed by a UX architect and a hackathon domain expert over two review rounds, every one of 160 features placed, clickable prototype per screen and state, today’s screenshots kept as the before.

Grok SIM-346 re-test fixes, organiser screens (group R2): Event page honours a #section link (scrolls to it, opens it if collapsed) and Save basics now shows ‘Saved’; People's no-applications note names the real stage (‘Sign-up open’); Teams keeps the Tracks section open and in the order just saved across Add/Save/Remove, the Fill teams preview only warns when the apply actually placed people differently than previewed, and the Teams list never says ‘Looking for members’ on a full team; Judging's Open-mode Progress no longer counts an organiser who hasn't actually scored; the Panel assignment grid warns and blocks Save when the saved mode isn't Panel, matching Manual's own warning; Results' stale-snapshot note only shows once scores have actually changed since publishing, and Show scores now says teams always see their own score (owner decision); Event page, People, Teams and Results all read read-only with one note (‘This event has ended. Settings can't change any more.’) once the event is archived, keeping only what the API still allows and is still useful (downloads, Directory, Publish). Added shared ui.js helpers: ui.possessive (a name ending in s gets a bare apostrophe, not ’s) and ui.zoneAbbr (a short zone name -- WIB/WITA/WIT/JST/KST/SGT/IST/GMT-BST/CET-CEST/US ET-CT-MT-PT -- where Intl's own short name is just a bare GMT+N offset), which ui.dateTime({zone:true}) now uses everywhere instead of Intl's raw suffix. Cosmetic #6: organiser phone tap targets (.btn, .btn.sm, the Menu button) raised to a 44px floor.

Grok SIM-346 re-test fixes, round 3 (groups R1/R3 parity + the retest-review's own findings): the classic voting-settings page gets a small in-page scrim/dialog confirm carried in its own script, since the restyle that moved the vote and voting-settings pages onto the app kit (round 2) also dropped the site chrome window.shConfirm needs -- narrowing who can vote while existing votes would be removed no longer throws. Track order is now persisted on the server: saving tracks gives each one a distinct created_at in the submitted order (no schema change), so a reload, the public page, the track picker and the judge panel grid all show tracks in the order they were saved, including after reordering existing ones -- the client-side-only reorder workaround in organiser-teams.js is gone. The event page header's Sign in/Home swap now checks location.host against the AppURL host: the old localStorage check only ever worked on the app's own origin, so a signed-in visitor at the event's own canonical URL (a different origin) always saw 'Sign in' wrongly offering 'Home' -- that host now always shows 'Sign in', linking at the app's sign-in page. The judge walkthrough's untargeted card moved to the bottom-right of the content area on desktop so it never covers Home's own 'Not open yet' card (kept above the phone tab bar / sticky save bar on phone, from round 2). A judge on an ended-but-never-locked event now sees 'Event ended' instead of 'Scoring not open'. The Event page's #section links are read with getElementById on a decoded hash instead of querySelector(location.hash), so an odd hash can no longer crash the whole render. The vote page's own zone labels now share ui.zoneAbbr's familiar-zone table (copied in, with a comment pointing at ui.js) instead of trusting Intl's raw short name, and the Go public page's hackZoneAbbr was given the same table plus a GMT+N fallback instead of ever falling back to the bare IANA zone name -- all three surfaces read a zone the same way now. ui.zoneAbbr's own GMT+N fallback no longer claims 'GMT' for a zone it can't compute an offset for (falls back to Intl's raw short name instead), and the dead 'Asia/Denpasar' entry (not a real IANA zone) was removed from its table. Saving Event page basics now refreshes the shell (ctx.refresh()) so a changed title or time zone reaches the switcher, sidebar, status bar and document.title -- the 'Saved' toast still survives the repaint via its existing re-place timers. Results' 'Scores have changed' note no longer shows when the preview read itself failed. Nits: ui.possessive('') (and this page's own copy in the vote page) now returns '' instead of a bare apostrophe-s for an empty name; Teams' 'membership changed since the preview' message is a plain note now, not an error alert, and the apply still shows 'Saved'; participant Home's pending-invite hero keeps the 'Entries close ...' note; the organiser's own event-website zip upload translates missing_index the same way participant-website.js already did; judge-scoring's 'No entry was submitted.' now also checks the video and code links before saying nothing was submitted.
